Definition: probably from G1166; right (as self-evident), i.e. justice (the principle, a decision, or its execution):--judgment, punish, vengeance.
BiblicalUsage: Dike is justice itself, the right sentence and the punishment that follows it. The islanders saw the viper fasten on Paul and assumed justice would not let a murderer live, and Jude holds up Sodom as an example of eternal fire. Paul warns that those who do not obey the gospel will be punished with everlasting destruction.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe justice is real and terrible, which is why the cross matters so much. Christ bore the sentence I deserved, so that justice is satisfied and mercy can reach me.
